newsitem.title: LATVIA: FREE TRADE AGREEMENT WITH TURKEY A TARGET.
newsitem.headline: FREE TRADE AGREEMENT WITH TURKEY A TARGET.

text.p: Latvia and Turkey are interested in signing agreements on free trade as soon as possible, the presidents of the two countries said on Thursday.
They made the comments on the last day of a visit by Turkish President Suleyman Demirel to the Baltics, which began Monday.
Oficials signed maritime deals and one on fighting organised crime and drug trafficking during a two-day visit to Latvia.
"Both sides are extremely interested in signing an agreement on free trade as soon as possible," Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis told a news conference.
Demerel said the legal foundation of relations between Latvia and Turkey were almost complete.
Apart a free trade agreement, the two sides needed to focus in the future on the avoidance of double taxation as well as the promotion of tourism and cultural ties, he said.
Latvian officials had earlier said more work was needed to co-ordinate the free trade deal in the food products and textiles sectors.
